reply: {"verses": [], "overall": "The translation follows the Latin closely in every verse: the elliptical opening (Fundamenta ejus) takes only a supplied copula, the Septuagintal genitives in 4 (Babylonis scientium me) and 7 (Sicut laetantium omnium habitatio) are kept rather than smoothed, and 'Homo, et homo natus est in ea' keeps the doubled 'homo' without explaining it. Tenses (ero, dicet, fundavit, narrabit, fuerunt) match. The pointing marks are the same and in the same order in all seven verses (one mediant each)."}
